data: © Soviet Academy of Sciences (historical). Landing site in Mare Fecunditatis. First robotic sample return (101 g lunar soil).
Descent stage with cabling, ascent stage launch base

First fully robotic sample return from another world — September 1970. Drilled into the lunar regolith with an articulated rotary drill, transferred 101 g of dust + small rock fragments into a sealed return capsule, then launched directly back to Earth without orbital rendezvous. Landed in Kazakhstan three days later. Two more Luna sample returns followed (Luna 20 in 1972, Luna 24 in 1976).
Proved end-to-end robotic sample return is feasible — the capability that underwrites Mars Sample Return today.

Luna 16 touched down in Mare Fecunditatis on September 20, 1970 — the first robotic sample return from another world, drilled 35 cm into the lunar regolith, sealed 101 g into the return capsule, and lifted off 26 hours after landing. The capsule landed in Kazakhstan three days later. Demonstrated that Soviet engineering could return lunar material without crewed flight, a year and two months after Apollo 11.
